Ukraine to Charge Russia in UN for Causing Humanitarian Disaster in Occupied City — Ukraine FM Sybiha urges UN intervention as Russia creates humanitarian catastrophe in occupied Oleshky (Kherson): 2,000+ civilians, incl. children, lack food, water, services; blocked aid/evacuation; people forage grass; FPV drones hunt them. Plot to Kill Russian Dissident: SBU Detains Hitwoman Sent via Belarus — Ukraine’s Security Service detained a woman accused of preparing to assassinate a Russian opposition figure who fought for Ukraine and now leads a nationwide civic organization. The SBU said Russia’s FSB recruited and trained the suspect in occupied Melitopol before sending her to Kyiv through Belarus.

Putin Plans to Visit APEC Summit, May Skip Trump’s G20 — Vladimir Putin plans to attend the APEC summit hosted by Xi Jinping in China but is likely to skip Donald Trump’s G20 gathering in Florida, Bloomberg reported on Monday. His expected absence would also eliminate a possible venue for direct talks with Volodymyr Zelensky.

The case is the latest in a series of cases in which Russia has tried to recruit Ukrainians to activate Starlink terminals after Kyiv’s new verification system in February, while Russia’s alternative, Rassvet, continues to suffer troubled launches.

The sanctions require unanimous approval from all 27 EU members and are due to expire at midnight on Tuesday, unless an agreement is reached.

Sybiha: Belarus Helps Russia Carry Out Drone Attacks on Ukraine — Andrii Sybiha accused Lukashenko’s regime of directly supporting Russian drone attacks and backed sanctions proposed by Belarusian democratic leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya.

Black Sea Blockade Threatens Global Food Shock — Russian and Ukrainian wheat exports during the July-to-September harvest period are expected to fall to roughly half last year’s volume as attacks disrupt Black Sea shipping. The crisis has pushed wheat prices to three-year highs, strained Ukraine’s storage capacity and increased food-security risks for countries dependent on affordable grain.

France to Strengthen Ukraine’s Air Defense With Radars, Interceptors — France will supply Ukraine with radars and interceptor missiles as Kyiv faces intensified threats to its energy system ahead of winter. Macron’s announcement came after talks with Zelensky in New York and follows discussions with Trump on air defense, an energy-strike moratorium and possible peace negotiations.

Ukrainian Forces Use New STING S Interceptor to Down Russian Geran-5 — Ukraine’s new STING S interceptor has shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran-5. The system is undergoing combat trials, with Wild Hornets planning mass production after testing.

Stay – and Lose Control: Auchan, Nestlé and Leroy Merlin in Russia — Russian assets of Auchan and Nestlé, as well as the legacy Leroy Merlin, were transferred to the temporary management. CARTOON: The Way Sanctions Should Work — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Moldova Seeks Energy, Water Emergency Over Critically Low Dnister Levels — Moldova is seeking emergency powers as critically low Dnister River levels threaten water and energy supplies. Authorities warn of potential shortages as the country remains reliant on imported energy, while the river’s decline has been compounded by drought, irrigation needs, and a Russian strike on a Ukrainian hydropower facility.

Ukrainian Drone Swarm Strikes Key Russian Oil Refinery in Samara — Dozens of Ukrainian drones targeted industrial facilities in Russia’s Samara Oblast overnight, reportedly striking a major Rosneft refinery and triggering a large fire, as Kyiv continues its campaign against Russia’s oil-refining infrastructure.

US Army Acquires Long-Range Ukrainian Surveillance Drones in $10.6m Deal — The U.S. Army will acquire Ukrainian-developed Raybird reconnaissance drones under a $10.64 million contract with Skyeton. The drones, capable of 24-hour flights and long-range surveillance, have been used extensively by Ukraine for intelligence and targeting. The deal highlights Ukraine’s growing expertise and expanding defense industry, shaped by extensive battlefield experience in drone warfare.

Zelensky, Macron Discuss Energy Moratorium Ahead of Trump Meeting — Zelensky met Macron in New York as Kyiv pushes for stronger air defense and reciprocal de-escalation ahead of talks with Trump.

Russian Ballistic Strikes Hit Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad, Kill 4 — Russian forces struck industrial sites in Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad during an overnight ballistic attack, killing two and wounding three people in Dnipro.

Macron, Trump Discuss Interceptors for Ukraine and Energy Truce — Macron pressed Trump for faster missile interceptors for Ukraine and discussed a possible reciprocal moratorium on Russian and Ukrainian energy strikes.

Tsikhanouskaya Warns Against Belarus Trade as Trump Looks Beyond Canada for Potash — Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya warned Washington against expanding trade with Minsk as Trump pursues a major Belarusian potash deal aimed at securing supplies for less than the US currently pays Canada.

Moscow Oil Refinery Halts Crude Processing After Sunday’s Drone Strike — Russia’s Moscow Oil Refinery has halted crude processing after a Ukrainian drone strike damaged key units at the facility. Zelensky said the attack targeted oil and logistics infrastructure supporting Russia’s war effort.

Ukraine Repels 197 Russian Attacks on Monday — According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU), Russia launched 197 attacks over a 24-hour period ending 10:00 p.m. local time on Monday, Sept. 21, focusing on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes. Thousands of kamikaze drones and at least 168 aerial guided bombs (KABs) were used by Russian armed forces to launch a sweeping barrage.

Hungary Refuses to Join Ukraine’s C8 Cooperation Initiative — Ukraine launched the new Carpathian Eight (C8) cooperation initiative to deepen security, energy and investment with regional members on Friday. While initial reports named Hungary as a member, the country’s Prime Minister Péter Magyar said Monday that Budapest declined the invitation and will not join the format. Hungary’s Foreign Ministry confirmed the position.

Ousted Prosecutor General Kravchenko Resigns From Prosecution Service — After “Operation Carthage” reached senior officials in his office, Ruslan Kravchenko lost the leadership post of prosecutor general. However, he remained a prosecutor until his latest resignation on Monday, even as President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree ousting him mid-September.

Ukraine Sets New Hospital Rules Amid New Two-Level Air Raid Alert System — Ukraine’s government has approved new rules for hospitals operating under the newly imposed two-level air raid alert system. During yellow (drone) alerts, facilities may remain open, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said. EU Extends Russia Sanctions for 3 Years, Delists 2 Oligarchs — While EU ambassadors have finally agreed to extend sanctions on nearly 3,000 Russian individuals and entities after several failed attempts, the new sanctions will not include the previously disputed oligarchs, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman. The decision has raised frustration among member states, while Kyiv condemned the move as unacceptable.

Russian Attack Destroys Pet Retailer Warehouse in Kyiv Region — A Russian overnight missile and drone attack destroyed a major warehouse belonging to Suziria Group in the Kyiv region. Company co-owner Polina Kosharna confirmed that no employees were injured during the strike, though emergency services remain at the scene to evaluate the full scale of the damage.

Russia Destroys Ukrainian Production Facility of World-Leading Ventilation Systems — In the early morning of Sept. 20, a Russian drone and missile attack destroyed the main Kyiv-region manufacturing facilities of Vents. As a global leader in ventilation equipment, the company is now assessing the severe damage to restore its production and logistics operations.

Russia ‘Unfortunately Lost Control’ of Its Diesel Refineries, Trump Says — Trump said on Monday that Russia has “unfortunately lost control” over its diesel production and called for the war to end. The comments came a day after a call with Zelensky and a day before the two’s meeting, with Trump having previously attempted to pin the blame for rising global diesel prices on Ukrainian strikes.

Russia’s ‘Partial Mobilization’ Turns 4: Is Another Draft Coming? — Four years after Vladimir Putin announced “partial mobilization,” Russia relies primarily on contract recruitment but also uses conscripts, prisoners, regional quotas, and administrative pressure to sustain its war. Ukrainian intelligence says slowing recruitment could push the Kremlin toward another call-up after the State Duma election, although no final decision has been independently confirmed.

Kernel Pilots Modular Grain Storage to Cushion Export Disruptions — Kernel installed the first modular grain store developed by a Ukrainian manufacturer at its request and filled it with 3,400 metric tons within two days. The company wrote that the design holds 3.5 times more than polymer grain bags in the same area. Kernel has bought units to add 40,000 tons of storage, which it plans to open to other producers.

EU Threatens Sanctions Over Russia’s Sham Elections in Occupied Ukraine — The EU condemned Russia’s parliamentary elections in occupied parts of Ukraine as a violation of international law and pledged sanctions against those involved in staging the vote.

Fedorov Says Zelensky Rejected His Election Proposal Because Zaluzhny Would Run — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said he personally proposed holding presidential elections in June and that President Zelensky was initially prepared to proceed. US Army Buys Battle-Tested Ukraine Observation Drone — The US Army awarded Skyeton $10.64 million for Raybird reconnaissance drones, Ukraine’s first major military-drone export to the US. The Raybird is combat-proven, while another Ukrainian UAV, the F10, underwent US Army testing.

Russia Hits 2 Gas Stations on Kyiv-Lviv M06 Highway — The highway served as an artery between Kyiv and the country’s western border, with both gas stations hit on the section within the Zhytomyr region west of Kyiv. The attacks followed Russia’s escalated campaign against Ukrainian gas stations.

Moscow Fortifies Power Plant After Record Ukrainian Attack — Moscow’s CHP-8 power plant is being surrounded with concrete blocks that could support anti-drone netting, according to eyewitnesses cited by ASTRA. The work follows the largest reported Ukrainian aerial attack on Moscow, which damaged the Russian capital’s major oil refinery.

After State Elections: Can Merz Keep His Job? — Germany’s CDU suffered major losses in state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, while Die Linke and AfD gained ground. The results have intensified questions over Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s leadership and the stability of Germany’s political centre. European media warn that growing polarisation could affect Germany’s role in Europe and support for Ukraine.

Ukraine Urges Europe to Send Patriot Missiles Now, Replenish Stocks With Future Production — Ukraine is proposing that European countries transfer Patriot missiles from existing stockpiles and replace them later with newly produced interceptors. Kyiv is also seeking faster access to bilateral funding commitments as the cost of the war rises.

Drones Target Major Russian Oil Hub 1,600 Kilometers From Ukraine — Drones reportedly attacked Ufa in Russia’s Bashkortostan region on Monday, potentially targeting oil infrastructure belonging to Bashneft, one of Russia’s largest refining complexes.

Book Genocide: How Russia Has Waged War on Ukrainian Books for Centuries — Russia’s campaign against Ukrainian books has a long history – from bans on publishing to modern attacks on the country’s publishing infrastructure. EU Fails to Agree on Putin Sanctions Renewal — EU ambassadors again failed to agree on extending individual sanctions against nearly 3,000 people and entities linked to Russia’s aggression against Ukraine. Ukrainian Combat Medics Show Sweden How Drones Save Lives — Combat medics from Ukraine’s 1st Separate Medical Battalion took their MAUL armored unmanned ground vehicle to Sweden where they shared their techniques for using the technology to rescue casualties from within the “kill zone” on the modern battlefield.

Russian Strike Torches Historic Zaporizhzhia Heritage University — An overnight Russian attack on southern Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia burned down Building 3 of the city’s main university. Frontline Update, Lyman Details, AFU Reorganization — The front line has moved in Ukraine’s favor in the northern Lyman sector, whereas the southern city of Orikhiv, in the Zaporizhzhia region, is bracing itself for an expected Russian push. Whitaker emphasized that boosting manufacturing in the US and Europe is key to meeting Kyiv’s air defense needs.

Ukraine, Russia, Hard to Reconcile on Black Sea, Turkish Minister Says — Ukraine and Russia maintain positions on Black Sea security that are “difficult to reconcile,” Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said following Ankara’s proposal to halt strikes on commercial shipping. Fidan confirmed that both Kyiv and Moscow responded to Turkish initiatives aimed at securing grain transit, but noted substantial differences remain.

Russian Strikes Kill Mother, 3 Children in Kyiv Region — Russian strikes on Kyiv region late Saturday, Sept. 19, killed a woman and three young children in the Fastiv district, regional authorities reported. The strike hit a private residential property as the children were going to bed, damaging homes and injuring several civilians. Concurrently, Russian forces struck the city of Dnipro, hitting the Novyi Kontynent shopping center and sparking a major fire that injured at least four people.
